- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to avoid missing downside momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast peak.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.33 to -0.33 within 3 days), model fails to mean-revert; force a 3–5 day mean-reversion bias toward historical 14-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts late-period (days 20–30) prices; reduce final 5–7 days by 3–8% to reflect diminishing momentum.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses direction; align forecast slope with sentiment direction (e.g., if sentiment rises, forecast must rise; if sentiment falls, forecast must fall).
